text:
maya: rolling a canary to prod 2.1.9 now — noticing token/sec drop on ctb across a subset of pods, blocking full rollout :warning:

adrian: saw the alert too, that's the same cluster where kernel fallback got enabled last night?

sophie: correct, merge 0f3a4b7 toggled kernel_selector heuristic for long-seq models, flagged in the release notes but not in the rollout playbook

maya: numbers: baseline ~420k tokens/sec, canary pods at ~270k token/sec, traffic-shift paused at 10%

ryan: rough profiler snippet from one affected pod:
```
CPU: 32 cores, GPU util 76%
ctb queue depth: avg 28 -> 110 ms queue latency
batch size dist: 1-3x spike in tiny batches (<=4), previously mode was 12
KV cache hitrate: 93% -> 72% on same trace
kernel chosen: fallback_fast_gemm (long_seq_path)
```

adrian: KV hitrate drop smells like a cache-key canonicalization change. Did the merge change request fingerprinting?

maya: investigating request id hashing now. repro on staging with curl + header replay shows same pattern

sophie: also seeing the continuous-batcher draining heuristic fire more often, causing smaller batches. suspect the new kernel_selector increases per-request latency which feeds back into the batcher deadline calculation

ryan: nailed a small repro. If kernel_selector prefers fallback_fast_gemm, p50 kernel latency goes +8ms for prefix length ~128, forcing CTB to close windows early. Patch 0f3a4b7 changed threshold from 200 to 120 tokens.

maya: that explains smaller modal batch size. smaller batches => more GPU kernel launches => throughput down. Can we test reverting the threshold locally?

adrian: created a quick branch reverting threshold to 200 and ran a short perf run on canary nodes: tokens/sec recovered to ~410k in the same traffic shape

sophie: sweet. we should bisect to the minimal offending change — it might be the threshold change or a related micro-optimization in kernel selection that introduced overhead on the decision path

maya: will hold rollout. marking as rollout-blocker and pinging infra for an emergency revert if we decide to go that route :hand:

perf-bot: CI perf regression detected on master at 1894998000: `ctb_throughput_test` dropped 34% relative to baseline. Candidate commits: 0f3a4b7, 0f3a9c2, 0f3aef1

ryan: running git bisect now between 1894950000..1894999000 with perf harness attached, will post results

adrian: while bisect runs — quick mitigate option: tweak batcher_deadline multiplier to +30% to bias bigger batches. That buys time but increases p99 latency slightly.

maya: prefer revert until we understand correctness risk. small p99 increase acceptable for short window? ops/clients might disagree though.

ryan: bisect result: first bad commit 0f3a9c2 — it's the commit that optimizes kernel selection path but inadvertently made the decision more synchronous (added a lock around selector cache) causing latency amplification under high concurrency

adrian: oh nice catch. lock contention explains spike in per-request latency and CTB deadlines firing early. so it's not the threshold change alone — it's the sync patch in 0f3a9c2 + threshold tweak in 0f3a4b7 that together regress throughput

sophie: recommended action: revert 0f3a9c2 immediately, open an RPC/async selector refactor. leave threshold as-is for now (200).

maya: I've queued an emergency revert PR for 0f3a9c2 and will hold canary. Deploy-bot, please keep canary at 10% paused.

deploy-bot: Canary pause acknowledged (canary=10%) — reverting commit 0f3a9c2 to staging candidate

ryan: post-revert perf on staging: tokens/sec back to 395-415k, KV hitrate stable at 92%, CTB batch sizes returned to mode ~12. Latency p50 unchanged vs baseline

adrian: great. follow-up: we'll remove the lock, replace with lock-free LRU or atomics, and add a microbenchmark for selector path to catch future regressions in CI (CTB throughput test should include high-concurrency kernel_selector warmup)

maya: creating a follow-up ticket to harden CI: ensure `ctb_throughput_test` runs in PRs that touch kernel selection and batcher heuristics. assign to ryan/adrian/sophie.

maya: tl;dr: rollout blocked, root cause = sync lock in kernel selector (0f3a9c2) + threshold tweak amplified effect (0f3a4b7). emergency revert applied, monitoring.

adrian: adding a short note to the release channel and changelog pointing to the revert + upcoming refactor. :memo:

sophie: thanks all — leave this thread for postmortem notes, will add profiling slices and flame graphs to the ticket.

maya: monitoring looks stable, unpausing traffic only after we see 30m stable window. for now keeping blocked. :lock:
